headline: Wet, windy stretch expected, with coastal flooding risk peaking Wednesday and Thanksgiving.
summary: A busy storm track is sending a series of Pacific weather systems toward Western Washington, steered by a fast jet stream, high-altitude winds that carry storms. Each stays offshore, but a stronger front aimed at the region midweek brings the worst of it. A brief break is possible in between, of uncertain length. Wednesday and Thanksgiving look worst, with several inches of rain possible in the Olympics, gusty coastal winds, and a wet, breezy few days in the lowlands. High surf and some of the highest tides raise the risk of major coastal flooding, and the Skokomish River may reach flood stage. Forecasters are fairly confident in the wet pattern through Thursday and early next week, though the longer-range forecast is less certain.
